audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Global level comparison omits the quadratic shift cost; Increment entropy bound loses the absolute base value; Concentration lemma threshold misses an entropy scale
limitations: P01 — Global level comparison omits the quadratic shift cost — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Continuous-path conclusion follows analytically; numerical five-point probabilities are only discrete-grid calculations.

P01 — Global level comparison omits the quadratic shift cost — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Small delta comparison is repaired by Cdelta+C'delta²+log2/T; limiting local continuity is not refuted.

P01 — Global level comparison omits the quadratic shift cost — Counterevidence: Small-delta bound is repaired on each fixed bounded delta interval with P02's corrected lower probability input. Theorem4 explicitly invokes Lemma1.1 on source p34. Core auxiliary/proof error; no final-theorem counterexample claimed.
P02 — Increment entropy bound loses the absolute base value — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Source images explicitly include absolute values.

P02 — Increment entropy bound loses the absolute base value — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Anchored increments plus Gaussian correlation yield positive q, then exponential lower bound; final Lemma2.22 not disproved.

P02 — Increment entropy bound loses the absolute base value — Counterevidence: This restores the ell>0 conclusion of Lemma2.22; fractional-power small-mass Lemma2.20 can absorb the retained base standard deviation using bounded total mass. Original operative chain into Lemma2.23 still invalid as printed; Major does not mean false final small-ball theorem.
P03 — Concentration lemma threshold misses an entropy scale — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Counterexample obeys all lemma hypotheses; no path simulation.

P03 — Concentration lemma threshold misses an entropy scale — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Actual downstream processes have stronger derivative/scale restrictions; their final propositions not disproved.
P04 — False low-frequency removed-mass estimate — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Reversing the printed inequality conflicts with required largeL regime.
P04 — False low-frequency removed-mass estimate — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Smooth only high-frequency tail and include low-frequency mass in base avoids this step.
P05 — Spectral projection fails for an origin atom — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Both denominators nonzero; not an empty-bin convention.

P05 — Spectral projection fails for an origin atom — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Separate zero atom and reflected positive-negative bins repairs Hilbert projection; rank-one cost does not alter singular ball exponent.
P05 — Spectral projection fails for an origin atom — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Counterexample not claimed to satisfy extra Prop5.3 mass constraints.
P06 — Rapidly oscillating density does not have the claimed averaged limits — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Pointwise oscillation is not averaged oscillation.

P06 — Rapidly oscillating density does not have the claimed averaged limits — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Theorem1 would yield existence for this same density, but its proof is not used as an independent proof of the final exponent.

P06 — Rapidly oscillating density does not have the claimed averaged limits — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Slow cos(loglog(e/|λ|)) provides different density with oscillating averages; persistence bounds need actual cited hypotheses.

P06 — Rapidly oscillating density does not have the claimed averaged limits — Counterevidence: Theorem1 and the displayed example cannot both hold, but no independent assertion of the final exponent is derived from the contested theorem. Checked replacement slow phase: log(1+log(1/u)/log(e/x))<=log(1/u)/log(e/x), integrable in u, so averaged and endpoint cos differ by O(1/log(e/x)). This proves only new averaged oscillations; persistence comparison and cited journal-version hypotheses remain unverified as disclosed.

P07 — Peripheral level and infinite-density ranges overstate positivity — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Main Theorem1 andProp2.25 correctly distinguish infinite density; examples agree with them.

P07 — Peripheral level and infinite-density ranges overstate positivity — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Restore ell>=0 in zero-density infinite-rate application and finite positive origin density inRemark3.

P07 — Peripheral level and infinite-density ranges overstate positivity — Counterevidence: These processes are allowed by M's infinite density definition. Restoring ell>=0 in the zero-density application and finite positive origin density in Remark3 avoids the examples. Theorem1, Remark2 and Prop2.25 retain the correct distinctions; no core proof reliance on these peripheral overstatements established.

Limitations: FFN reference journal version inaccessible in attemptedwebroute; primaryv2 checked explicitly.
Limitations: Not every cited theorem independently reproved; all main source read, dependencies examined.
Limitations: P03 full downstream uniform constants and P06 replacement probability bounds need repair; no mathematical acceptance implied.

proposition.claim:
Recorded check: Global level comparison omits the quadratic shift cost

Measure: (2pi)^-1 indicator[-pi,pi] dλ. Level: 0. T: 4. Alpha: 1/(4pi). A: 1. Beta: 1. B: 10. Delta: arbitrary positive; let delta tend to infinity.

Recorded check: Increment entropy bound loses the absolute base value

Measure: delta0, finite symmetric measure in logarithmic moment class. H: >0. Radius: 0.1.

Recorded check: Concentration lemma threshold misses an entropy scale

Epsilon: 0.5. A: 1. T: 16delta^-2. Variance: delta²/32. Spectral support d: sqrt96/delta. Process: smooth stationary uniform bandlimited spectrum.

Recorded check: False low-frequency removed-mass estimate

Mu: P01 measure. A: 1. Beta: 1. B: 10. Nu: indicator[-1/2,1/2] dλ. Alpha prime: 2. D: 0.5. L: eta^-2. T: 160L. Eta: sufficiently small for every fixed proposition constant.

Recorded check: Spectral projection fails for an origin atom

D: 1. N: 1. Measure: (delta_-1+delta0+delta1)/3, compactly supported purely singular. Bins: I1=[0,1],I-1=[-1,0).

Recorded check: Rapidly oscillating density does not have the claimed averaged limits

A: >0. B: >a. Density: [(a+b)/2+(b-a)/2 cos(1/λ)] indicator|λ|<=1. Final argument range: a<b/3.

Recorded check: Peripheral level and infinite-density ranges overstate positivity

Moving average: U0=1,U1=-1,all others0; square summable, sum0, Fourier transformcontinuous. Level: -1. Atom examples: delta0 and delta0+nonzero bandlimited ac spectrum, in L with infinite origin density.

Retained report, Problem 1: Problem 1 (P01: Major). Lemma 1.1, p. 7, claims a bound linear in every \(\delta>0\) with a constant independent of \(\delta\).

Retained report, Problem 2: Problem 2 (P02: Major). Lemma 2.19, pp. 14–15, bounds \(\mathbb E\sup_{[0,h]}|f_\rho|\) by a positive power of \(\sup_{[0,h]}|r_\rho(0)-r_\rho(t)|\).

Retained report, Problem 3: Problem 3 (P03: Major). Lemma 2.21, pp. 15–16, asserts that variance at most \(\varepsilon/T\) and increment variance at most \(a^2h^2\) imply…

Retained report, Problem 4: Problem 4 (P04: Major). In Proposition 3.1, pp. 21–23, the passage after source (3.9) uses \((1-h^2)\nu_{L/T}(\mathbb R)\le1/T\), claiming this follows when \(L\ge1/(2\alpha')\).

Retained report, Problem 5: Problem 5 (P05: Major). Lemma 4.2, pp. 25–26, allows every spectral measure supported on \([-D,D]\) but assigns zero asymmetrically to the first positive bin.

Retained report, Problem 6: Problem 6 (P06: Major). Remark 1, p. 2, and Section 5.4, pp. 41–42, advertise nonexistence of the zero-level persistence exponent for…

Retained report, Problem 7: Problem 7 (P07: Minor). Example 3 on p. 8 extends the zero-density conclusion to every real level.
